tested_scope_delta.overlap: Both are authority/fencing mechanisms around durable side effects and both prevent duplicate or conflicting state transitions by requiring a stable authority boundary before subsequent mutation.
tested_scope_delta.separation: AID-Guard governs provider-delivery lineage, terminal outcome discovery, recovery-horizon fencing, ambiguous-delivery handling and one-successor authorization for external effects. event_log_authority governs local canonical-log writer serialization, lock/error behavior and append/migration ordering. event_log_authority has no provider terminal-query, predecessor/successor transfer, exact-result replay or recovery-horizon semantics; AID-Guard does not provide the canonical events.jsonl writer lock, rotation ordering, tail-isolation ordering or migration-lock scope. Neither tested scope contains the other.

finding.reason: The strongest overlap is authority/fencing against duplicate durable effects, but the sealed mechanisms operate at different layers and enforce different invariants. Collapsing AID-Guard into event_log_authority would lose provider-outcome/recovery-lineage coverage; collapsing event_log_authority into AID-Guard would lose canonical-log writer serialization and migration contention coverage.
